transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

I'm here because... well, it's my job. I clean buildings. And lately, I just... I can't go into some of the rooms. The trash rooms, mostly. I just keep thinking I'm going to see a rat. Even when I know it's probably fine, I just... I can't do it. It's getting bad.
Is it only the trash rooms that you avoid, or are there other places or situations that also make you feel this way?

No, it's... other places too. Basements, storage rooms... laundry areas. The dumpsters out in the alley. 

I try to turn down those routes if I can. If I'm forced to do them, I just... I make sure to leave the door propped open. And I just rush through it as fast as I can. I just feel scared the whole time I'm in there.
Do you find yourself avoiding any open or public spaces, like parking lots, marketplaces, or public transportation, because of this fear?
No... I don't think so. I go to the store and take the bus just fine. It's really just... the places I told you about.
Do you ever feel anxious or avoid places because you're worried about being judged by others or feeling embarrassed?
No, not really. I don't care much about what people think. It's just... just the rats.
Is it specifically the thought of seeing a rat that scares you, or is it something else about those spaces that makes you anxious?

It's just the rats. I mean... that's why I'm here. It's gotten so bad I can't even do parts of my cleaning job anymore. Even when I know it's just a trash room or an old building, and... and it's probably not dangerous. But just the thought of seeing one... it's too much.
